Using arm-none-eabi-objdump and arm-none-eabi-nm from the same toolchain, we inspected the application objects and final ELF file for secret-dependent branches and memory addresses, fixed loop bounds, removal of countermeasure operations, and recombination of Boolean shares.

We perform four dudect-style tests covering polynomial multiplication during decryption and encryption, as well as both complete CCA2 operations. Each test collects 100,000 DWT measurements, divided equally between two classes, using the (n,q) = (256,256) firmware image.

Evaluation is limited to the tested binaries and components: fixed-versus-random timing, TVLA, and debugger-assisted single faults. Multi-target faults and electromagnetic or invasive injection are considered out of scope for this work.

The six selector-store and loop-control skip trials reveal a narrower integrity limitation: skipping the final store or loop control silently corrupts a valid output, so output-selection duplication or a loop-completion check remains necessary.
Sharing covers CPA decryption but not its surrounding oracle and re-encryption logic; fault results cover the tested single-point logical model.
